title: Rounding a Restated Auto Loans Rate by the Age of the Loan
content:
How a restated rate on a loan of the Auto Loans line is rounded follows how long the loan has been on the books, counted in whole months from the date it funded to the day of the restatement.

- At least 36 whole months: the restated rate is rounded down to the cent.
- At least 24 but less than 36 whole months: the restated rate is rounded up to the cent.
- Less than 24 whole months: the restated rate is rounded half-up to the cent.

## The same rate under each convention

Take a rate of 8.8449 before rounding. On a loan funded 44 whole months before the restatement it becomes 8.84. On a loan funded 28 whole months before it becomes 8.85. On a loan funded 10 whole months before it becomes 8.84, the third decimal being below the half.

Take a rate of 7.1250 instead. At 44 whole months it becomes 7.12; at 28 whole months it becomes 7.13; at 10 whole months it becomes 7.13, the half rounding upward.

## Where one convention gives way to the next

A loan funded exactly 36 whole months before the restatement is rounded down to the cent. A loan funded exactly 24 whole months before is rounded up to the cent. A loan funded 23 whole months before is rounded half-up to the cent.

## A rate already exact to the cent

The three conventions differ only in the cents, and two of them can move a rate that is already exact. A rate of 8.84 with nothing beyond the cent reads 8.84 under all three, because there is nothing left to round.
